doc.title: Operations on Strings
doc.para: Operations on Strings In TJS2, strings pseudo-exist as objects of the String class, but the String class does not actually exist, nor are they truly objects of the String class (however, using the typeof operator on a string returns "String"). However, by treating strings as objects, several methods and properties are available.

length The length property returns the length of the string. Please note that it is a property and not a method. However, you cannot assign a value to this property.
In TJS, all characters are handled internally as UNICODE, so full-width characters and half-width characters are both counted as 1 character.
var str = "abc漢字"; var n = str.length; // 5 is assigned to n var n = "abc漢字".length; // 5 is assigned to this as well

'Numeric' Properties By indirectly specifying a number as a property, you can access the character at that character position. For example, if str is a string or an expression representing a string, str[0] will be a string representing the first character. An exception occurs if the number is longer than the string length or if it is negative (however, an empty string is returned at the position past the last character).
You cannot generate assignment expressions.
var str = "abcdef"; var c = str[0]; // 'a' is assigned to c var c = str[2]; // 'c' is assigned to c str[3] = 'A'; // Error because assignment expressions cannot be generated var c = str[100]; // Error because the index is out of range var c = str[6]; // Empty string '' is assigned

charAt The charAt method returns the character at the specified position in the string. It works similarly to the 'Numeric' property, but if it is out of range, it always returns an empty string (does not throw an exception).
Syntax : charAt(<character position>)
var str = "abcdef"; var c = str.charAt(3); // 'd' is assigned to c

indexOf The indexOf method returns the position of a substring.
Syntax : indexOf(<substring>[,<search start position>])
Searches the string for <substring> starting from <search start position>, and returns the position where it was first found. Returning 0 means the beginning of the string. Returning -1 means it was not found. If <search start position> is omitted, the search starts from the beginning of the string.
var str = "abcdefghijkl"; var n = str.indexOf("fgh"); // 5 is assigned to n var n = str.indexOf("xyz"); // -1 is assigned to n

toLowerCase This method takes no arguments. toLowerCase returns a string with the alphabetic characters converted to lowercase. Full-width characters are not converted.
These methods do not affect the original string.
var lwr="ABCDEF".toLowerCase(); // "abcdef" is assigned to lwr
In the current version of TJS2, conversion is performed only for characters with character codes less than 0x80.
toUpperCase Opposite to toLowerCase, this method returns a string with lowercase alphabetic characters converted to uppercase.

substring The substring method returns a substring of the string.
Syntax : substring(<start character position>[,<character count>])
Returns a substring of the string starting from <start character position> for <character count> characters. It does not affect the original string. If <character count> is omitted, all characters after <start character position> are returned. Note that the meaning of the arguments is different from the method of the same name in JavaScript.
var ss="abcdefghijkl".substring(3,3); // "def" is assigned to ss

sprintf The sprintf method formats a string.
Syntax : sprintf(argument, argument, ....)
Treats the string as a format string and returns a string with text formatted similarly to sprintf in C language. It does not affect the original string.
var formatted = "%04X %c %5d".sprintf(v1, v2, dic[v1]);

replace The replace method performs string replacement.
Syntax : replace(<pattern>, <replacement string>)
Replaces the string according to the regular expression pattern and returns the string after replacement. It does not affect the original string. For details on operation, please refer to the replace method in .

split The split method splits a string.
Syntax : split(<pattern/delimiter set>, <(reserved)>, <ignore empty elements=false>)
Returns an array object containing the results of splitting the string.
Please also refer to the split method in (note the order of arguments).

escape The escape method converts a string into a format that can be represented inside a TJS string literal. Symbols such as \ and " are all escaped using the \ symbol so that they are not interpreted for special purposes.
Syntax : escape()
Returns the escaped string. It does not affect the original string.
var escaped = str.escape(); // " in str is converted to \", \ to \\, etc.

trim The trim method returns a string with leading and trailing whitespace removed. It does not affect the original string. Leading and trailing whitespace refers to characters with character codes U+0001 to U+0020. That is, it includes ASCII control characters and the like, but does not include so-called full-width spaces. If there are consecutive leading or trailing whitespaces, all of them are removed.
Syntax : trim()
Returns a string with leading and trailing whitespace characters deleted. It does not affect the original string.
var str = " Hoge ".trim(); // str is "Hoge".

reverse The reverse method returns a string with the sequence of characters reversed. It does not affect the original string. In the current version of TJS2, behavior is not guaranteed for strings containing UTF-16 surrogate pairs.
Syntax : reverse()
Returns a string with the sequence of characters reversed. It does not affect the original string.
var str = "Hoge".reverse(); // str is "egoH".

repeat The repeat method returns a string repeated the specified number of times. It does not affect the original string.
Syntax : repeat(count)
Returns a string with this string repeated count times. It does not affect the original string.
var str = "Hoge".repeat(3); // str is "HogeHogeHoge".
